content.text:
Implement the P0 accessible browser and voice-guided interface for Entire Echo
on branch feature/echo-web.

First read:

- docs/buildathon/initial-architecture.md
- the merged cmd/entire-echo implementation
- its ReviewBundle model and tests

Before editing:

1. Use Entire Graph search or definition lookup to locate the real ReviewBundle
   type, JSON field names, evidence type, card/finding type, terminal renderer,
   and current CLI entry point.
2. Verify every Graph finding by reading the corresponding source and tests.
3. Treat the merged Go model as the source of truth. Do not invent a parallel
   schema based only on the architecture document.
4. Report incomplete Graph output honestly.

Ownership:

Create only the static accessible interface and fixture under:

cmd/entire-echo/internal/webui/assets/

Prefer these files:

- index.html
- styles.css
- app.js
- review.fixture.json

Do not:

- modify checkpoint acquisition,
- modify Graph execution,
- change deterministic review synthesis,
- change terminal or JSON rendering,
- add the HTTP server or --web CLI flag,
- commit changes.

The integration owner will connect these assets later.

Data behavior:

1. In production mode, fetch GET /api/review.
2. Provide an explicit fixture/development mode using review.fixture.json.
3. Match the real merged ReviewBundle JSON shape.
4. Render warnings and unavailable evidence without hiding them.
5. Never turn missing Graph evidence into “no impact.”
6. Every factual claim must provide a “Show source” control using its evidence IDs.
7. Escape or use textContent for all checkpoint/transcript content; do not inject
   untrusted text using innerHTML.

Page structure:

1. Skip-to-content link.
2. Product title and one-sentence overview.
3. Target checkpoint/session/commit identifiers.
4. Linear numbered review cards:
   - Requested
   - Implemented
   - Missing or uncertain
   - Potentially affected
5. Continue safely section.
6. Evidence details.
7. Warnings/status region.
8. Voice playback controls.

Accessibility requirements:

- Semantic header, main, nav, section and heading structure.
- Full keyboard operation.
- Strong visible focus.
- No color-only meaning.
- Plain language and manageable line length.
- Comfortable default spacing.
- Reading-density selector: focused and detailed.
- Respect prefers-reduced-motion.
- Use an aria-live polite region only for short status updates.
- Do not auto-focus unexpectedly.
- Do not auto-advance cards.
- All voice behavior must have an equivalent visible keyboard control.

Voice-guided review:

Use the browser SpeechSynthesis API.

Speech must start only after explicit user action.

Support:

- Read current card
- Pause/resume
- Stop
- Repeat
- Previous card
- Next card
- Slower/faster rate
- Read evidence

Display which card is active and what will be spoken.

Do not add microphone recognition in P0.

If speech synthesis is unavailable, keep the complete review usable as text and
show a non-blocking message.

Visual direction:

Create a calm, clean, high-contrast developer interface designed for developers
with ADHD, dyslexia, or reading overload.

Avoid:

- dense side-by-side diffs,
- animated backgrounds,
- auto-scrolling,
- excessive gradients,
- tiny text,
- icon-only controls,
- long transcript dumps.

Testing and verification:

1. Verify fixture mode renders without the Go server.
2. Test loading, successful, empty, malformed and unavailable-data states.
3. Test keyboard navigation through every control.
4. Test focused and detailed density modes.
5. Test speech start, pause, resume, repeat, next, previous, rate and stop.
6. Test the speech-unavailable fallback.
7. Check the browser console for errors.
8. Test desktop and narrow/mobile widths.
9. Run git diff --check.
10. Do not modify unrelated files.

At completion report:

- Graph commands and results,
- source files used to verify the real schema,
- files changed,
- browser checks performed,
- accessibility decisions,
- known limitations,
- and integration requirements.

Do not commit.
I’ll first trace the merged CLI model through Graph and source/tests, then build only the static assets and exercise them in fixture mode—including failure and speech fallbacks.

content.text:
Implemented the static Entire Echo web interface under:

- [index.html](/Users/gayathriperumal/buildathon/cli/cmd/entire-echo/internal/webui/assets/index.html)
- [styles.css](/Users/gayathriperumal/buildathon/cli/cmd/entire-echo/internal/webui/assets/styles.css)
- [app.js](/Users/gayathriperumal/buildathon/cli/cmd/entire-echo/internal/webui/assets/app.js)
- [review.fixture.json](/Users/gayathriperumal/buildathon/cli/cmd/entire-echo/internal/webui/assets/review.fixture.json)

No unrelated files changed and nothing was committed.

Schema verification used [main.go](/Users/gayathriperumal/buildathon/cli/cmd/entire-echo/main.go) and [main_test.go](/Users/gayathriperumal/buildathon/cli/cmd/entire-echo/main_test.go). The UI matches `ReviewBundle`, `Target`, `Claim`, `Evidence`, and `Warning` JSON fields exactly; terminal rendering and the current CLI entry point were also verified there.

Graph work performed:

- `entire graph capabilities --json` — confirmed Go definitions and type relations are supported.
- `entire graph search ... ReviewBundle ...` — emitted no findings within its command window.
- `entire graph def ReviewBundle --repo . --format json` and the committed-tree variant — produced no records after over a minute and were stopped.

That incomplete Graph output was not treated as evidence; direct source and tests were the source of truth.

Browser QA performed with a temporary local static server:

- Fixture mode loaded successfully, including evidence, uncertainty, warnings, source controls, and identifiers.
- Production `/api/review` missing-data behavior showed a non-blocking unavailable state and fixture recovery control.
- Tested source disclosure, card activation, focused/detailed density, desktop and 375px narrow layout, native keyboard Tab traversal, and browser console errors (none).
- Exercised speech start, repeat, evidence reading, previous/next selection, and rate controls. Browser synthesis completed immediately in this environment, so pause/resume/stop could not be observed mid-utterance.
- `node --check`, fixture JSON parsing, untrusted-HTML scan, `git diff --check`, and `mise exec go@1.26 -- go test ./cmd/entire-echo` passed.

Accessibility decisions include semantic landmarks/headings, skip link, visible focus, keyboard-native controls, concise cards, non-color-only confidence labels, reduced-motion support, a single polite short-status region, no auto-focus/scroll/advance, and text-only insertion for all review content. Speech is always opt-in and has visible keyboard equivalents.

Known limitations: live malformed/empty payload and speech-unavailable states are handled by validation/fallback code, but could not be simulated through the intentionally absent HTTP integration. The integration owner needs to serve these assets and provide `GET /api/review` returning the versioned `ReviewBundle` JSON.
